legend.summary: Lightning seen from the International Space Station from March 2017 to July 2023, in 14 equal parts, in order. A scan line crosses the world once per part, west to east.
legend.method: Everything you hear sits on the scan line. Places in the north sound higher and in your left ear; places in the south sound lower and in your right. Listen to the storms swing north and south and back again as the seasons turn, about seven times.

items.meaning: Places with a lot of lightning, played as the scan line crosses them. Louder = more lightning.
All the lightning under the scan line. It is quiet over calm ocean and swells over stormy land like Central Africa or the Amazon.

legend.caveat: Values are read from the colours of NASA's video, not from the satellite measurements, so they are relative. The sensor sees only from about 55 degrees north to 55 degrees south. NASA's movie has no dates, so the parts are equal stretches of the movie, not calendar months.
